subject: Request: pin + auto-evacuate canary policy for latency SLO mitigation
messages:
From: Priya Kaur <pkaur@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenLine Health SRE <sre@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Rolling request: Pin + auto-fallback during canary (latency SLO risk)

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from our side — we are preparing a canary of the GLH checkout personalization model next week and we want to bake in explicit safeguards that preserve our 99.95% uptime / p95 latency target. Our concern: small traffic spikes during the canary might push up tail latency.

Ask: can Redwood enable a temporary "pin + auto-evacuate" policy for this canary? The behavior we want is:
- Pin the production model version for the majority of traffic;
- Route a 5-10% canary cohort to the new variant;
- If p95 latency for the canary exceeds baseline by >30% for 5 consecutive mins OR error-rate >1%, automatically evacuate canary traffic back to pinned prod version and leave the pin in place until manual review.

Attached: canary-config-proposal.pdf and latency-slo-sheet.csv with our baseline numbers.

We need this in place early next week. Can you confirm feasibility and whether we need any SLA exception paperwork?

Thanks,
Priya
Principal PM, GreenLine Health
priyaa.k@greenlinehealth.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Kaur <pkaur@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling request: Pin + auto-fallback during canary (latency SLO risk)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. This is feasible; we'll need a short internal authorization to allow an autorevert/evacuate policy that overrides the standard auto-scaling routing for the canary cohort.

High-level plan I propose:
1) Redwood will create a pinned production variant for your account (version lock) during the canary window.
2) A 7% canary cohort will be routed to the new model variant.
3) Telemetry triggers (p95 delta >30% sustained 5m OR error-rate >1%) will activate an automatic evacuate that immediately switches the canary cohort back to the pinned production variant and keeps the pin.
4) We will log the event, open an incident in your HubSpot deal thread, and create a rollback ticket for joint postmortem.

Marcus — can you confirm the config knobs (threshold debounce, cooldown window, and whether we need a short SLA carve-out to cover the auto-evacuate behavior)?

Priya — we'll also attach the exact JSON policy we intend to deploy for your review. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow morning to finalize thresholds.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kaur <pkaur@greenlinehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling request: Pin + auto-fallback during canary (latency SLO risk)

On Sun, Apr 25, 2027 at 11:02 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus — can you confirm the config knobs (threshold debounce, cooldown window, and whether we need a short SLA carve-out to cover the auto-evacuate behavior)?

Hi all — technical details below. We have an execution-ready policy that maps to Redwood's routing layer. Summary:
- Canary cohort: 7% traffic (configurable).
- Triggers: p95_canary / p95_prod > 1.30 for 5m continuous OR canary_error_rate > 0.01 for 3m continuous.
- Debounce: evaluate on 1m buckets with a 5m sliding window.
- Cooldown: once evacuated, cool-down 30m before retrying a canary; manual unlock required after 3rd repeated evacuation in 24h.
- Pin semantics: pin prevents automatic model substitution for pinned traffic; pinned traffic will continue hitting the production variant while canary cohort is isolated.
- Telemetry & audit: we log reason, pre/post p95 numbers, tokens served, and snapshot KV cache size in the event payload.

SLA carve-out: This does not change your uptime SLA for pinned traffic. The only change is that canary cohort can be auto-evacuated which may mask new-variant improvements for the cohort until we manually re-open. From Redwood's side, we can sign a short amendment stating that auto-evacuate actions are operational mitigations and not SLA violations for pinned production traffic. If GreenLine needs this in a formal agreement, we can route it through Legal.

Attached is the policy JSON sample (inline excerpt):
{
  "policy": "canary_auto_evacuate_v1",
  "canary_pct": 0.07,
  "trigger_p95_ratio": 1.30,
  "trigger_error_rate": 0.01,
  "evacuate_cooldown_minutes": 30
}

If everyone is ok with the thresholds, I can schedule the rollout gate and enable the policy in the staging stack for a smoke test tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kaur <pkaur@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling request: Pin + auto-fallback during canary (latency SLO risk)

Thanks Marcus — this reads well. A couple of governance points before I give operational approval:
- Approve the proposed thresholds (p95 ratio 1.30, error-rate 1%).
- Require that any evacuation event automatically creates a JIRA incident and notifies GreenLine SRE and our on-call infra lead.
- If we perform more than 2 evacuations for the same canary within a 24-hour window, require a manual hold and customer sign-off to re-open.

For the SLA paperwork: we are ok to provide a short amendment that clarifies auto-evacuate is an operational safety mechanism and does not count as a production SLA breach for pinned traffic. Priya — please confirm whether GreenLine prefers a standalone one-page amendment or a short addendum to the existing contract. If you want the standalone, I'll loop Legal and get a draft sent today.

Once we have confirmation on the paperwork preference, Marcus — please run the staging smoke test and share the telemetry dashboard link in the thread.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

We'd like the staging smoke test today and the production window scheduled for Friday Apr 30th at 02:00 UTC. Please confirm when the staging link is available and confirm the final JSON policy artifact so we can sign off.

Thanks — Priya
